candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: use appropriate organizational and referral resources, coordinate transfers, and participate in quality-improvement systems.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — interpreting stroke-center certification for referral and transfer
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret Comprehensive Stroke Center certification as evidence that a hospital has met an advanced, externally reviewed stroke-care framework with stroke-specific standards, evidence-based care processes, and performance measurement, while continuing to verify real-time transfer capability for the individual client.

options.A: The hospital has met Joint Commission advanced stroke-certification requirements that include core disease-specific standards plus additional stroke-specific requirements, evidence-based clinical practice processes, and performance measurement.
options.B: Any hospital can use the CSC designation regardless of stroke resources, patient volume, standardized care processes, or certification review.
options.C: CSC is a basic rehabilitation-only designation and does not indicate an advanced acute-stroke program.
options.D: CSC certification means performance measurement is unnecessary once the initial certification review is passed.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The Joint Commission classifies Comprehensive Stroke Center certification as an advanced stroke certification developed with the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association. Advanced certification requires the core Disease-Specific Care requirements plus additional clinically specific requirements, use of evidence-based clinical practice guidelines, and ongoing performance measurement. B, C, and D contradict the certification framework. Specific transfer decisions still depend on the patient's clinical needs and the receiving hospital's current capabilities and availability; certification does not replace real-time transfer assessment.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Joint Commission CSC certification is an advanced stroke-care certification requiring compliance with disease-specific and stroke-specific standards, evidence-based care processes, and performance measurement; it is not an unrestricted label available to any hospital.
candidate.source_document_title: Stroke Certification; What Is Certification?; 2026 Stroke Certification Standards
candidate.source_locator: Stroke Certification — Comprehensive Stroke Center is one of the Joint Commission's advanced stroke certifications; advanced programs meet core Disease-Specific Care requirements plus additional clinically specific requirements. Certification Standards — certification framework includes standards, clinical practice guidelines, and performance measurement. What Is Certification? — eligible programs use standardized evidence-based care methods and performance measurement to improve over time. 2026 Stroke Certification Standards contains the requirements to achieve and maintain CSC certification.
